decision.reason: I was unable to verify or refute this finding because the working tree is not readable from my environment. Glob("**/*") and Glob("*") at the stated cwd (/tmp/stage-repo-jpdy7b/repo) returned no files; Read of /tmp/stage-repo-jpdy7b/repo/package.json reported "File does not exist"; Grep for `resolveRange` across /tmp/stage-repo-jpdy7b returned no matches; and Glob for **/package.json under /tmp returned nothing. (The path the original reviewer cited, /tmp/eval-item-hRoO8Z/repo, likewise does not exist for me.) I therefore could not read packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts, packages/sheets/antlr/Formula.g4, packages/sheets/src/store/memory.ts, or packages/sheets/src/formula/arguments.ts to confirm that resolveRange substitutes only omitted endpoints, that ROW/COL are legal standalone range endpoints, or — critically — whether a size cap already exists inside toSrefs/extractReferences/fetchGridByReferences or at the parser level (which would be an `already-guarded` refutation). Refuting requires a named ground plus file:line locations I actually read; I have neither. The finding is in files the PR did touch (coordinates.ts, memory.ts, arguments.ts, Formula.g4 are all on the authoritative changed-file list), so `pre-existing` does not apply either, and unbounded range expansion driving memory/CPU exhaustion amplified to every collaborator is plausibly in-lane as a resource-exhaustion / unsafe-input-handling weakness rather than a pure correctness bug. Per the rubric, uncertainty keeps the finding, so I confirm it at low confidence and flag that a downstream verifier with filesystem access should specifically check for an existing cap in toSrefs / extractReferences / buildDependantsMap before treating this as blocking.
